name: A Five-Vertex Face Whose Vertices and Edges Are Retainable but the Face Is Not
definition: Start with the certified positive family $Y_2$ that retains a marked square but does not peel to it, attach a leaf at one square vertex in a fresh coordinate, and let $K$ be the square together with the new leaf. Form the one-sided peripheral expansion $(T\times\{0\})\cup(H\times\{1\})$ over the four-vertex path $H$.
properties: $K$ has the five-vertex shape $H\cup\{2\}$ from the smallest canonical four-edge face type. The family $T$ peels to every vertex and every edge of $K$ but not to $K$. The expanded piece is positive with connected exterior and fails to peel to its common face, while every proper exclusive-coordinate image does peel to that face.
